source_excerpts.text:
## 1. Operation and hypotheses

There are N finite isothermal lumps, with C_i>0, and one fixed-temperature bath b. The positive, time-independent, reciprocal conductances form a tree on these nodes and b. Write all temperatures relative to the bath. At t=0 a finite energy E is deposited at one source lump s: T_s(0)=E/C_s and all other T_i(0)=0. No further input, switching, advection, other storage degree of freedom, or feedback occurs. The source-connected component after deleting the bath contains every relevant node; any other nodes are wasted capacity and can only weaken the bound stated with totals.

Let L be the Dirichlet weighted Laplacian with the bath deleted and C=diag(C_i). Then

    C dT/dt = -L T.

The normalized energy flux into the bath is f(t)=sum_i g_ib T_i(t)/E. Positivity, stability, and energy conservation imply f>=0 and integral f=1. Define

    tau = integral t f(t) dt,
    sigma^2 = integral (t-tau)^2 f(t) dt,
    R = (sum_i C_i)/C_s.

The coefficient sigma/tau is the width of the deterministic release waveform. It is not an assertion about stochastic experimental timing noise. The absorption-time representation is a mathematical tool: normalized node energies p_i=C_i*T_i/E obey a killed reversible continuous-time Markov equation.

## 2. Theorem

For N>=2 and R>1,

    sigma^2/tau^2 >= B_N(R)
      := 1/[1+(N-1)tanh(log(R)/(2(N-1)))].                 (1)

This is the exact minimum over all such trees with N lumps, prescribed C_s, total capacity R*C_s, and any prescribed tau>0. Equality is attained by the positive ladder below. Thus neither branching nor arbitrary positive optimization of heat capacities and conductances can improve (1) in this class.

At fixed R, even arbitrarily many lumps obey

    sigma^2/tau^2 >= 1/[1+log(R)/2].                       (2)

For a target relative width epsilon<1, a necessary condition is

    R >= exp[2(epsilon^(-2)-1)].                          (3)

The exact finite-N feasibility condition is sharper. A finite R is possible only if epsilon^2>1/N. In that case the sharp necessary and sufficient capacity requirement in this ideal class is

    log R >= 2(N-1)*atanh[(epsilon^(-2)-1)/(N-1)].

Sufficiency follows from the attaining design and continuity/monotonicity of B_N(R). Equality epsilon^2=1/N requires R to diverge.

source_excerpts.text:
## Model

A single source reservoir has constant heat capacity C, temperature rise T0 above a fixed bath, and initial energy E=C*T0. It cools through an autonomous memoryless conductance G(T), with

    0<g_min<=G(T)<=g_max,    K=g_max/g_min>1.

There is no subsequent input or independent clock. The normalized bath-flux distribution is the full released energy, including off-state leakage. Let its mean be m and variance V. Overall timescale rescaling does not change V/m^2.

Writing u=T/T0 and z=-log u, conservation says normalized released energy is -du. Therefore Z=-log U is an Exp(1) variable and the release-time random variable is

    t(Z),  t(z)=integral_0^z a(s)ds,
    a(s)=C/G(T0*exp(-s)).

Rescale time so a is in [1/K,1]. This is an exact representation of the model, not a stochastic material mechanism.

## The exact global optimum

Among every measurable conductance curve in the allowed range, the smallest squared coefficient of variation v=V/m^2 is the unique solution v in (0,1) of

    2[atanh(v)-v] = -log(1-1/K)-1/K.                     (1)

An attaining memoryless curve is a single threshold: G=g_min initially, then G=g_max after the reservoir cools to eta*T0, where

    eta=(1-v)/[(1+v)(1-1/K)].                           (2)

For continuous curves with no bound on slope this is an infimum, approached by steep smooth transitions. A real actuator with bounded transition width/dynamics may do worse. The theorem optimizes the mathematical conductance curve; it does not supply a physical curve that was not measured.

## Derivation for a threshold

Let d=-log eta, a=1 before d, a=1/K afterward, and r=1-1/K. Its survival function has off-state decay until d and on-state decay afterward. Direct integration gives

    m=1-eta+eta/K,
    E[t^2]=2[1-eta(1+d)+eta(d/K+1/K^2)].                (3)

Set y=r*eta. Then m=1-y and E[t^2]=2[1-y(1+1/K+log(r/y))]. Differentiating E[t^2]/m^2 with respect to y shows the unique stationary point satisfies

    1+1/K+log(r/y)=(3-y)/(1+y).                         (4)

The derivative of the left side minus right side is

    -(1-y)^2/[y(1+y)^2]<0.

It tends to positive infinity at y=0 and is negative at y=r, so the root is unique in the physical interval. At this point

    v=(1-y)/(1+y).

Substituting in (4) gives (1),(2). All endpoint cases have CV squared 1, so this is the unique threshold optimum.

## Q17

**Original versus reviewed claim.** The initial question was a sharply timed substantial heat release using passive ordinary conduction/storage. The rejected equal-rate directed cascade both assumed an unavailable one-way primitive and used an established Erlang principle. The replacement actually constructs reciprocal components and proves

`CV² >= [1+(N-1)tanh(log(R)/(2(N-1)))]^(-1)`

for all fixed positive reciprocal thermal trees, with initial energy confined to one source lump. This is a genuine family theorem, not a selected fixture. The limit `CV² >= 1/(1+log(R)/2)` establishes the exponential capacity penalty for the specified RMS metric.

**Proof audit.** In [Q17/PROOF.md §§3–6](../../review_material/Q17/stage1/PROOF.md), I reconstructed the ladder cofactor/product transform, exponential-kernel inverse, positive equality weights and concavity step. The tree Green-function calculation preserves the mean under branch collapse and adds exactly the displayed nonnegative second-moment term. The degenerate one-node collapsed path is the exponential case. These steps support the stated tree theorem; they do not establish the open looped-graph extension or narrow-window concentration.

**Independent checks.** Spectral integration of the actual bath-flux waveform on 16 attaining ladders (`N=2,3,7,16`, `R=1.1,3,80,10000`) agrees with the claimed CV² within `3.31e-12`. Sixty fresh tree collapses agree with the variance-gap identity to `3.56e-13` relative error. Twelve independent continuum boundary-value transfer solves agree within `3.31e-14`. Replaying `explore.py` and `verify_continuum.py` also reproduces the supplied results. Ordinary free-capacity/free-resistance multistart synthesis matches the construction, including CV² `0.310271805518` at `N=8,R=100`; there is no demonstrated synthesis-performance gain.

**Strong antecedents and disposition.** [Aldous–Shepp's primary abstract](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/15326348708807067) establishes unrestricted phase-type/Erlang optimality. [Chiclana, Appendix A, Theorem A.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17513v1#A1) gives the adjacent reversible-chain variance bound in effective-resistance/terminal-conductance resources; I read its statement and derivation.
